correctness.rationale: The sorted-denominator inequalities force (x,y) in {(2,3),(2,4),(2,5),(3,3)}, with finite exact z ranges, and modular valuation cancellation proves each q in (6/7,1) has reduced denominator divisible by 2 or 3. A totient ratio in that gap has only primes >=11 in its support, hence a reduced denominator coprime to 6, contradiction. Equality 6/7 requires 7|n and forbids any other prime; all 7-powers attain it by (2,3,42). The strict versus weak boundary and exclusion n=1 are explicitly verified. Exact finite checker independently matches all bounded arithmetic tests; it is not the proof of the infinite claim.
